message.content:
Paris has many iconic landmarks, but if you’re looking for **the single “most famous” spot**, it’s almost always the **Eiffel Tower** (La Tour Eiffel).  

*Why it stands out:*  
- It was built as the centerpiece of the 1889 Exposition Universelle and instantly became a symbol of French ingenuity.  
- Every year millions of visitors climb its iron lattice structure—or simply enjoy the view from below—to see the glittering lights at night.  
- Its silhouette is recognized worldwide; it appears in countless films, photographs, postcards, and even logos.

Other contenders often mentioned alongside the tower include:

| Landmark | Why it matters |
|----------|----------------|
| **Louvre Museum** | Home to thousands of masterpieces—including the Mona Lisa—making it one of the world’s largest art museums. |
| **Notre‑Dame de Paris** | A masterpiece of Gothic architecture, famed before the fire and still a pilgrimage site. |
| **Sacré‑Coeur & Montmartre** | Offers panoramic views over Paris and embodies bohemian history. |

But when people think of *“Paris”*, the image that pops up first is usually the sparkling Eiffel Tower against the skyline.
